newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC in talks with Channel 5 over launch date.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC in talks with Channel 5 over launch date.

text.p: Britain's Independent Television Commission is in discussions with Channel 5, the country's fifth terrestrial television station, to set a new launch date, an ITC spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

"We are in discussions with them again about a new date," an ITC spokeswoman told Reuters. It is up to Channel 5 to ask the ITC for a new launch date, she said, adding that there has never been an agreement to delay the launch until February.
The ITC would like to know "fairly soon" when Channel 5 wants to begin broadcasting, the spokeswoman said.

Channel 5 has been scheduled to debut on January 1, 1997. Its plans were complicated last month when it was granted access to a new frequency, which will make the station available to another 1.8 million homes -- boosting the station's coverage to 80 percent of the UK population. The change, however, has increased Channel 5's task of retuning video recorders to prevent interference from the new signal.
A spokeswoman for Channel 5 recently said that chief executive David Elstein would write to the ITC this week to suggest a new launch date.
Channel 5 is a consortium headed by British media companies Pearson Plc and United News & Media Plc and also including Luxembourg broadcaster group CLT and U.S. investment group Warburg Pincus.
